newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow cuts 96/97 sugar output to 123.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow cuts 96/97 sugar output to 123.5 mln T.

text.p: World sugar production will reach 123.48 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, down 850,000 tonnes from a previous estimate, trade house Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
Output in 1995/96 was 123.19 million tonnes, it said in its latest monthly report.
Consumption requirements were expected to reach 121.00 million tonnes, against 118.66 in 1995/96, with much of the expansion concentrated in the Far East and Asia, it added.
Czarnikow said the figures implied a rise in world stocks of 1.73 million tonnes, with 750,000 tonnes considered as a disappearance factor.
World sugar stocks rose by 3.89 million tonnes in 1995/96 with a disappearance factor of 650,000 tonnes.
Although the revised 1996/97 estimates showed only a small overall change in expected sugar production, some individual countries, particularly in Asia, showed sizeable swings.
Total cane sugar output was forecast at 86.06 million tonnes, 728,000 tonnes lower than last year but 2.32 million tonnes lower than the previous estimate issued in November.
India was expected to produce 15.00 million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97, sharply down from the record 17.88 million turned out a year earlier.

The Czarnikow report cited excessive payment delays for delivered cane, which had prompted farmers to switch cane land to alternative crops, plus a slow start to milling and dry conditions in some growing areas.
In its previous estimate, Czarnikow pegged Indian output at 16.30 million tonnes.
It also reduced production forecasts for Thailand and the Philippines.
Thai output was expected at 6.42 million tonnes, up from last year's 6.32 million but lower than the earlier estimate of 6.64 million.

Crop prospects had slipped back in the Philippines although consumption was expected to remain strong at 2.05 million tonnes, 50,000 more than last year. Output was pegged at 1.85 million after 1.78 million in 1995/96.
Brazil was still expected to turn out another record sugar production but less than previously expected.
Czarnikow scaled back its Brazilian output figure by 250,000 tonnes to 14.60 million tonnes, which was still 1.01 million more than in 1995/96.
